description: Table 1 is a single two-row, eight-column composition table rendered as a raster image, captioned "Chemical composition of the tested steel (wt.%)." The header row lists the elements in the order C, Si, Mn, Al, Cr, Mo, Ni, Fe; the single data row gives 0.35, 0.26, 1.47, 4.50, 0.26, 0.28, 1.47, Bal. There is only one specimen column, so the table characterises one steel, not a series; no standard deviations, detection limits or duplicate analyses are printed. Al at 4.50 wt.% is by far the largest alloying addition, followed by Mn and Ni (both 1.47 wt.%), with C 0.35, Si 0.26, Cr 0.26 and Mo 0.28 wt.%; Fe is given as the balance. This Al-rich, low-C base chemistry is what makes the steel low-density and δ-ferrite-forming, the premise on which the rest of the paper builds. The citing text states that this steel was fabricated by vacuum induction melting (VIM), homogenised at 1200 °C for 4 h, hot forged to 40 mm and air cooled, and that specimens were subsequently reheated to 650, 750, 850 or 950 °C for 2 h and hot rolled with 60 % reduction from 40 mm to 16 mm, giving samples named R650, R750, R850 and R950. The table itself carries no processing information; all heat-treatment and rolling conditions come from the citing text and are listed here for completeness.

subfigures.description: A one-row composition table (wt.%) with header C, Si, Mn, Al, Cr, Mo, Ni, Fe and values 0.35, 0.26, 1.47, 4.50, 0.26, 0.28, 1.47, Bal. Single specimen; no error values printed.

observations.observation: The table image contains one header row and one data row only, i.e. it reports a single steel composition, not a set of alloys.
The header row reads exactly C, Si, Mn, Al, Cr, Mo, Ni, Fe and the data row reads 0.35, 0.26, 1.47, 4.50, 0.26, 0.28, 1.47, Bal.
Al is the largest alloying addition at 4.50 wt.%, more than three times the next largest additions Mn = 1.47 wt.% and Ni = 1.47 wt.%.
C is the lowest alloying element listed at 0.35 wt.% and Fe is reported as the balance (Bal).
No uncertainty, standard deviation, repeat-analysis or detection-limit values are printed anywhere in the table.
The caption states that Table 1 gives the chemical composition of the tested steel in wt.%.
The citing text states the tested steel was fabricated via VIM (vacuum induction melting).
The citing text states the ingot was homogenised at 1200 °C for 4 h, hot forged to 40 mm thickness and air cooled to room temperature.

The citing text states specimens were heated to 650 °C, 750 °C, 850 °C and 950 °C, held 2 h, then hot rolled with a 60 % reduction ratio from 40 mm to 16 mm, giving four sample groups named R650, R750, R850 and R950.
The citing text states the designed temperature range covers carbide precipitation/dissolution (≤750 °C) and DRX and DIFT (≥850 °C).
